transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-01-05 15:00 PST | Duration: 55m | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
Attendees: Eric (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Alex (Ceres CTO), Priya (Platform Eng), Jordan (Procurement)

Summary: SE walked through a compatibility pattern for Ceres Skyway's LLM Gateway. Discussed VPC peering, KMS/HSM expectations, model fallbacks, and quantization impacts. Decided on benchmarks and doc exchange.

[00:00] Eric: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick intros, i'm Eric from Redwood, this is Maya our solutions engineer, and i think Alex you wanted to start with your constraints?
[00:12] Alex: yeah thanks, uh so quick context, Ceres Skyway is building an LLM gateway to front internal apps, we need a marketplace listing so our customers can spin up a Redwood-backed backend or bring their own private deployment. main constraints: strict data residency, requirement to use our HSM in prod for key wrapping, and p99 latency target of ~120ms for short prompts.
[00:33] Maya: got it. just to clarify, when you say HSM for key wrapping, do you mean Cloud HSM or an onprem HSM behind your VPC? or both?
[00:42] Alex: onprem HSM behind VPC, vendor is... i keep saying the name wrong, it's an older one, um, SafeKey, S A F E K E Y, not cloud HSM.
[00:52] Maya: okay that helps. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS integrations, we have a KMS adapter pattern that can call out to an onprem HSM via a proxy. there are a few auth handshakes to validate on initial key import. i'll share the adapter docs. (link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/kms-adapter)
[01:10] Priya: and about networking, we will do VPC peering and have a transit gateway in the middle; are there any special ports or keepalives you need for the Redwood runtime? we are on a fairly locked down egress policy.
[01:24] Maya: we require outgoing TLS to the Redwood control plane for metrics and rollouts; for private we can toggle telemetry off but the runtime needs to reach the control plane on port 443 for heartbeat and rollout checks. data plane traffic for inference stays inside the VPC if you pin to private, so no public egress for tokens.
[01:42] Alex: good. can you confirm whether the KV cache and prefix caching will work with our gateway pattern? our gateway shards requests and does local caching.
[01:52] Maya: yes, Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching, but the cache sync pattern depends. if you run multiple runtime pools in different AZs you'll want a shared redis or memcache for hot prefixes. note, there's a subtlety with continuous batching and your gateway's request coalescing—if the gateway pads sequences it can blow up batch efficiency.
[02:14] Priya: yeah we do pad to 64 tokens for now to simplify pooling. is that bad?
[02:20] Maya: it hurts throughput a bit. for quantized models, sequence length variance affects kernel selection; padding short requests to 64 will reduce throughput/cost efficiency. propose: gateway should send real prompt lengths and let the runtime batch. we can provide a header example.
[02:36] Eric: quick interjection, also important for marketplace listing: we need to make sure the L4 load balancer health checks are compatible with the listing helm chart – some customers run 30s health checks which trip cold start fallbacks.
[02:50] Jordan: from procurement side, we need to see SSO / SAML integration and SOC2 docs before legal will sign anything. can you drop those?
[02:59] Eric: yes i'll send SOC2 and our ISO pack and marketplace checklist after the call.
[03:05] Alex: on model variants - we plan to offer a hosted fallback for small customers. what's the policy for automatic fallback if private capacity is exhausted?
[03:15] Maya: you can configure routing policy by region and tier; default is to fail open to a compatible hosted variant in the same model family, but we can set an explicit canary to route X% to hosted and only route on capacity exhaustion. also TTLs and cache invalidation matter if you switch variants.
[03:35] Alex: ok can we get a configuration example?
[03:38] Maya: yes, i'll include a sample routing policy in the runbook.
[03:42] [04:00] Maya: now the fun part: quantization. you mentioned int8 vs bfloat16, can you share what accuracy delta you're comfortable with?
[04:09] Priya: for most of our agents, up to 1% top-line metric drop is ok, but for compliance flows we can't have hallucination increases. any guidance?
[04:20] Maya: when you move to int8, you often see small generation variance; we'll run evals using your prompt sets. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles per workload. i'll run a quick bench: int8 static vs dynamic vs bfloat16. results go to you.
[04:36] Alex: how long do those benchmarks take?
[04:39] Maya: initial microbench is few hours; full eval with your prompt set is ~48hrs to get stable numbers. i'll prioritize microbench to unblock architecture.
[04:49] [05:00] Eric: talk about orchestration — during upgrades we do canary rollouts, but customers like Ceres want rollback-on-regression to be automatic. what are the hooks?
[05:10] Maya: we integrate with tracing and can wire your eval metrics into rollout gating. if quality drops beyond threshold we can auto-roll back to previous model. there is a small window where KV cache warming leads to transient quality dips, so thresholds should account for that.
[05:28] Priya: are there any known issues running the runtime with our network appliance (we use NetFort X, it does deep packet inspection)?
[05:37] Maya: DPI can interfere if it terminates TLS or rewrites headers. runtime expects end-to-end TLS to the model-serving container. if NetFort is TLS-terminating you'll need a pass-through rule or mTLS. we support mTLS between runtime and model shards.
[05:55] Alex: can we see the helm chart and the values we should change for marketplace listing?
[06:00] Maya: yes, i'll send the helm chart link and a marketplace packaging checklist. (artifact: repo link: gitlab.redwood/internal/partners/ceres/helm-values.md)
[06:12] Jordan: procurement note: pricing tiers and dedicated commit numbers matter. can you give rough committed capacity pricing?
[06:20] Eric: i'll give a ballpark in the follow-up, we don't want to lock numbers on this call.
[06:26] [06:30] Alex: what about telemetry and PII? our logs sometimes include hashed user ids; we need to ensure telemetry filters before it leaves our VPC.
[06:38] Maya: for private we can disable runtime telemetry or configure filters at the agent. we recommend sending minimal metrics to control plane — only health and anonymized counters. we'll share the telemetry config snippet.
[06:52] Alex: one more technical, cold-start time for large models with quantization - what's the p90 cold start?
[06:58] Maya: depends on model size and disk speed; with pre-loaded checkpoints on NVMe we're seeing p90 cold start of ~4-6s for 7B-ish models with quant, bigger models 10-18s. but warm invocations are sub-100ms token latency typically.
[07:20] Priya: acceptable. can the gateway surface model-level metrics in our prom endpoints? we'd like per-tenant token counters.
[07:29] Maya: yes, runtime exports Prometheus metrics; you can scrape per-tenant counters if you run per-tenant pods or use labels. we'll include the metrics list.
[07:42] [08:00] Alex: are there any restrictions around supporting our custom auth headers and an authz webhook?
[08:07] Maya: we support authz webhooks; the runtime can call your endpoint to validate a token, but you'll want low-latency SLO for that hook; otherwise use a local cache/memoization layer at the gateway.
[08:22] Priya: our authz endpoint has a 20ms p95 right now, should be okay.
[08:28] Maya: perfect.
[08:30] Eric: ok let's recap next steps.
[08:33] Maya: i'll run the hybrid throughput microbench (int8 vs bfloat) using a synthetic mix that matches your 60/30/10 short/medium/long split, and post results to the shared repo.
[08:44] Alex: i'll send the VPC peering diagram, exact HSM vendor details and sample latency numbers.
[08:51] Jordan: legal/procurement will expect SOC2 and SAML samples, procurement will wait for those before sending initial PO.
[08:58] Eric: i'll attach SOC2 and marketplace checklist and a draft SLA.
[09:04] Maya: i will also add a sample routing policy for canary/fallback and the helm values to the repo.
[09:12] Alex: timeline wise, if we get the docs this week we can run an internal POC and target onprem demo around Jan 18.
[09:20] Eric: great, i'll schedule the demo for the week of Jan 18 and invite you all.
[09:26] [09:30] Priya: small thing - when you share benchmark configs please include the exact docker image tags and quantization flags so we can reproduce locally.
[09:36] Maya: yes 100%, will include image sha and flags.
[09:40] Jordan: cool thanks all.
[09:42] Eric: thanks everyone, we'll follow up, meeting adjourned.
